📌 Governance Snapshots: Why Your Tokens May Not Count in a DAO Vote

Main Points
⏺ Some DAOs calculate voting power using token balances from a specific blockchain block
⏺ Buying tokens after that snapshot may not increase your voting power
⏺ This post explains how balance snapshots work and why purchase timing matters

1️⃣ Core Idea — the protocol records balances at a selected block to determine how many votes each participant receives.
2️⃣ Why It Exists — a fixed reference point prevents voting power from changing every time tokens are transferred during the voting process.
3️⃣ Example — a vote uses balances from block #1000, but you buy tokens at block #1005. Those new tokens won't increase your voting power for that proposal.
4️⃣ Risk Surface — users may buy governance tokens specifically to participate, only to discover the snapshot already happened.
5️⃣ Practical Rule — before buying governance tokens, check the snapshot block, delegation conditions, and voting eligibility rules.

Final Thoughts

DAO governance isn't only about how many tokens you hold. It can also depend on when you held them. Sometimes your voting power is decided before the vote even begins.

Bypassing Israel, sharing the profits

A Gulf-Europe route through Syria would bypass Israel. Some of the investors positioned to collect the fees come from countries that also back the route through Israel. Competing geopolitical visions can share a portfolio.

Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shaibani said Saturday that Damascus is discussing entry into the Mecca defense pact linking Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan. Membership remains under consideration. Syria has acquired no automatic defense guarantee.

The transport plans are more concrete. Turkey and Saudi Arabia are planning a $5.5 billion rail link through Jordan and Syria. It would give Gulf freight another route toward Europe without requiring Israeli transit. Technical studies and missing infrastructure still stand between the announced corridor and through-running trains.

At Syria’s Mediterranean outlets, the concessions are already signed. France’s CMA CGM holds a 30-year concession for Latakia’s container terminal. Abu Dhabi’s AD Ports agreed to acquire a 20% stake in the Latakia operation for $22 million. 

Dubai’s DP World has a separate 30-year concession at Tartus, with an $800 million investment program. 

France and the UAE also support IMEC, the proposed India-Europe corridor whose planned route includes Israel. Their companies’ commercial presence in Syria complicates the picture of two neatly opposed blocs.

A Syrian corridor could compete with Haifa for future freight. 

The immediate advantage belongs to the logistics companies, which are positioning themselves to handle the cargo whichever diplomatic route succeeds.

➡️ Pi Network has released four updates covering app development, token tracking, AI-assisted software packaging, and identity verification ahead of its Nov. 17–19 Ecosystem Summit.Inside the Developer Portal, a dedicated App Configuration section has replaced the previous onboarding checklist. Developers can manage domains, API keys, app wallets, and privacy information from the same area.

📊 Navigation now provides clearer routes to services including Pi Sign-In, Ecosystem Listing, PiNet and the Pi Ad Network, according to the team. For approved applications, local storage lets preferences and session information remain on a user’s device. Pi said the data stays off its servers, although it remains tied to the particular account and device and does not automatically follow users across devices. 

⚡️ The September release placed documentation on a single Pi-owned domain, bringing together resources previously spread across SDK documentation, a community guide and GitHub. Its guidance covers registration, sandbox development, authentication, payments, and preparing an application for Mainnet.

Have you ever wondered why modern medicine focuses almost exclusively on chemical intervention, while ignoring the physics of the human body?

In 1934, at the Scripps Ranch in San Diego, a discovery was made that could have changed the course of human history. This is the story of Royal Raymond Rife and the “Mortal Oscillatory Rate.”

How Can You Use This Today?

Administrative work is taking time away from patient care. For every hour physicians spend with patients, they spend two more on paperwork.

A study that tracked U.S. doctors throughout their workdays found they devote just 27% of their time to direct patient care. Nearly half goes to electronic health records and billing. Even during appointments, doctors spend more than a third of each visit looking at a screen—and many finish their notes at home.

It’s no wonder visits can feel rushed and 4 in 10 physicians report burnout. The problem has persisted for a decade, but hospitals are beginning to test tools that could ease the administrative burden, including AI note-taking and digital medical scribes.

[Sinsky, C., Colligan, L., Li, L., Prgomet, M., Reynolds, S., Goeders, L., Westbrook, J., Tutty, M., & Blike, G. Allocation of physician time in ambulatory practice: A time and motion study in 4 specialties. Annals of Internal Medicine, 165(11), 753–760]
